title: The temporary fix that shipped
prompt: A security review flags this image: "container process runs as UID 0". The author insists they switched to the `node` user. Select the line that makes the container run as root, and think about what the right fix for the original error would be.
hints: The last `USER` instruction before `CMD` decides who the container runs as.
The real need was one writable directory, not root for the whole process.
explanation:
Line 11 switches back to root after `USER node`, so the process starts as UID 0. The original `EACCES` came from `/app` being owned by root. Create the one directory the app writes to, hand it to the app user, and stay non-root:

```dockerfile
RUN mkdir -p /app/tmp && chown node:node /app/tmp
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]
```
Even better, have the app write to `/tmp`, which is writable by every user and can be a `tmpfs` mount when the root filesystem is read-only.
